transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... I guess I'm here because I just have this... constant restless feeling. Like I'm wound too tight, I suppose. 

I just can't fully settle down. Even when I'm supposed to be sitting calmly, like through a planning meeting at work... or trying to paint, or do yoga. I just... yeah. I can't really settle.
When you feel this restless, wound-up feeling, is your mind also racing with worries or concerns, or is it more that your body just feels like it needs to move around?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't really noticed if I'm worrying about anything specific. It's mostly just... a physical feeling, I guess. Like my body just needs to shift around.
How long have you been experiencing this restless, wound-up feeling? Has it been going on for most of your life, or did it start more recently?

Um... I guess it's been noticeably harder to manage for about two years and two months now. Just... well, some conflicts with my in-laws started taking over a lot of our evenings around then. So... yeah. About that long.

Besides the physical restlessness, do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things in your life — like your health, finances, family, or work — or is the worry not really a big part of what you're experiencing?
Um... no. Not really. I don't think worry is a big part of it. It's mostly just... the physical part, like I said.

Looking back to your childhood and teenage years, did you have similar trouble sitting still or focusing in school, or is this restlessness something that really started around the time these in-law conflicts began?

Um... well... I guess it didn't just start recently. 

I mean... back in elementary school, I used to get notes sent home. Just... for popping out of my seat, mostly. And... I guess I had a habit of talking over the other kids, or rushing to answer before the teacher was even done asking the question. So... yeah. I suppose it's been there for a while.

latest_inference.note: Patient reports lifelong history of restlessness, inability to sit still, impulsivity (talking over others, rushing to answer), and difficulty focusing - all consistent with ADHD. F06.8 (other specified mental disorder due to known physiological condition) and F48.8 (other specified nonorganic mental disorders) are ruled out as the symptom pattern is classic for ADHD rather than secondary to medical condition or somatization.
